fatal_errors: The proposed eutectic fcc/B2 HEA is not the target CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 self-lubricating composite.
The hypothesis replaces Mo-content variation and spark-plasma sintering with an unrelated 5 GPa HPHT treatment.
No solid-lubricant, silver, oxide, molybdate, tribofilm, or glaze mechanism is proposed.
The predicted outcomes concern tensile strength and ductility rather than temperature-dependent friction and wear.
The falsification experiment contains no sliding, friction, wear, counterface, atmosphere, or tribofilm measurements.
The cited evidence supports mechanical strength-ductility behavior, not wide-temperature self-lubrication or the stated numerical improvements.
explanation: The response has only broad thematic overlap through the use of a high-entropy alloy and a nominal 25–800 °C range. It does not reconstruct the target composition, Mo-dependent sigma-phase strengthening, SPS processing, or the transition from MoS2/Ag lubrication to high-temperature oxide and silver-molybdate glazing. Its baseline and quantitative strength/ductility predictions are not substantiated by the supplied excerpts. Although tensile testing could discriminate its mechanical claims, it cannot establish suitability as a self-lubricating material because no tribological test is included. The cited papers may support EHEA strength and ductility, but they do not validate the central self-lubrication claim.
